title: Cross-Device Session Continuity Library
description: Library to seamlessly continue wallet sessions across devices (top non-trading product unlock)
problem_en: Wallet sessions don't persist across devices — switching mobile→desktop forces re-auth and loses transaction state. No standard XRPL session library exists despite this being identified as the top non-trading product unlock.

title: Institutional Multisig Wallet (Full UI)
description: Safe-equivalent for XRPL — full UI for institutional multisig
notes: Distinct from gap-01 (treasury platform) — kept separate
problem_en: XRPL supports multisig natively but there's no Safe-equivalent UI for institutional treasury teams. Manual coordination via raw transactions is unworkable for funds, DAOs, and corporations holding XRP.

title: Smart Contract Wallet on EVM Sidechain
description: ERC-4337 wallet — table-stakes vs Base/Arbitrum
problem_en: XRPL EVM Sidechain lacks ERC-4337 account abstraction wallets. Without smart accounts (social recovery, gas sponsorship, batched txs), EVM Sidechain UX is years behind Base/Arbitrum where AA is table-stakes.

title: Unified Cross-Chain Wallet SDK
description: Single SDK supporting both XRPL native + EVM Sidechain
problem_en: Developers building cross-chain products on XRPL native + EVM Sidechain need two separate wallet integrations. No single SDK abstracts both chains' signing, accounts, and queries.

title: Institutional Data Emission Adapter Library
description: ISIN/CFI/LEI/FIX/IFRS adapters — highest leverage
problem_en: Institutional systems require ISIN/CFI/LEI/FIX/IFRS data formats; XRPL emits its own format. Every institutional integration rebuilds this adapter from scratch — a massive duplicated cost across adopters.

title: Stablecoin Accounting & Reconciliation Export
description: QuickBooks/Xero/IFRS-compatible export library — narrow scope (kept as BLOCK)
notes: Narrow lib — gap-10 is the broader APP that uses this
problem_en: Merchants accepting RLUSD/USDC need to reconcile transactions with QuickBooks/Xero. No export tool exists today, blocking merchant adoption since accountants reject unreadable blockchain data.

title: Multi-Flow Institutional Access Control Library
description: Permissioned Domains × Credentials for institutional flows
notes: Distinct from gap-04 (user-facing KYC app) — kept separate
problem_en: Institutional flows require complex access control combining Permissioned Domains + XLS-70 Credentials. Implementing this composition is error-prone and rebuilt per project — a library would unblock multiple downstream use cases.

title: Pluggable Proof Primitives Library
description: Hash/signature/ZK/BYO-scheme — composable primitives
problem_en: Different use cases need different proof schemes (hash, signature, ZK). No XRPL library provides a pluggable framework, forcing each project to pick one and reimplement from scratch.

title: Treasury wallet B2B XRPL-native
description: Coinshift/Utopia Labs equivalent — B2B treasury platform (uses M-02 multisig as primitive)
notes: Added Phase 1 — distinct from M-02 (multisig) which is a primitive
problem_en: B2B treasury management (Coinshift/Utopia Labs-equivalent) doesn't exist on XRPL. Businesses holding XRP/RLUSD need workflows for invoicing, payroll, vendor payments, multisig approval, accounting export.

title: KYC reusable cross-app
description: User-facing identity passport — manage and reuse KYC credentials across XRPL apps
notes: Added Phase 1 — user-facing app distinct from M-07 (backend lib)
problem_en: Every XRPL app forces users to KYC again. Users hate repeating the same KYC across 10 apps. A reusable credential passport (XLS-70 DID) lets users KYC once and reuse everywhere.

title: On-chain accounting + reporting
description: Broader accounting/reporting platform (uses M-06 export lib + adds reporting/multi-currency)
notes: Added Phase 1 — APP layer above M-06 narrow export lib
problem_en: Beyond stablecoin export, companies need full accounting + reporting on-chain (P&L, balance sheet, audit trails, multi-currency). A platform consolidating XRPL on-chain activity into standard accounting reports.

title: Streaming payroll for DAOs and freelancers
description: Streaming payroll on XRPL — new concept (PayrollXRP blueprint)
notes: Added Phase 1 — new concept not covered elsewhere
problem_en: Monthly batch payroll doesn't fit modern work (DAOs, gig workers, global freelancers). Continuous stream payments make sense but no XRPL service exists. XRPL near-zero fees + fast finality = perfect substrate.

title: Hardware wallet integration for XRPL wallets
description: SDK/library enabling Ledger/Trezor hardware signing across XRPL wallets — currently zero support
notes: Added from Djason interview May 2026 — major institutional adoption blocker
problem_en: No XRPL wallet supports Ledger/Trezor hardware wallets natively. Serious holders can't use cold storage; institutions can't custody safely. Years behind Ethereum/Solana where HW wallet support is table-stakes. (Source: Djason interview, May 2026)

title: DeFi-first consumer XRPL wallet
description: Consumer wallet with first-class DeFi UX (2-click yield access, visible positions, smooth onboarding) — Xaman-replacement
notes: Added from Djason interview — Xaman DeFi UX is broken
problem_en: Xaman (the main XRPL wallet) has poor DeFi UX — too many actions to access yield, DeFi positions are unfindable, consumer onboarding is inadequate. No XRPL wallet treats DeFi as a first-class feature. (Source: Djason interview)

title: Vault Wrapper Pattern Library (XLS-65)
description: Timing arbitrage on XLS-65 amendment
problem_en: XLS-65 (Single-Asset Vault) is fresh from XRPL amendment process. Building on it requires understanding low-level vault mechanics. A wrapper library would let any builder ship vault products in days, not months.

title: Risk-Signal Aggregation from MPT Trading
description: Kennedy Reassurance — XRPL-native novel pattern
problem_en: MPT trading data contains valuable risk signals (Kennedy reassurance pattern, position dynamics). No aggregator extracts these signals, leaving them invisible to risk managers and lending protocols.

title: Lending Protocol on EVM Sidechain (Morpho-style)
description: Morpho-style lending — top community survey need
problem_en: Community survey ranks lending as #1 demanded primitive. EVM Sidechain has no Morpho/Aave-class lending. Without it, sophisticated DeFi capital can't flow into XRPL.

title: Uncollateralized Lending Interface (XLS-66)
description: UI for XLS-66 unsecured lending — Evernorth intent
notes: Merged with gap-08 (Lending senior tranches XLS-66)
problem_en: XLS-66 enables uncollateralized credit on XRPL. Evernorth announced intent but no interface exists. Borrowers and lenders have no way to interact without raw transaction crafting.

title: Compliant Credit Vault (institutional service)
description: Agent-curator with attestations — A1 Tier 1 #1
problem_en: Institutional lenders need credit vaults with attestation-based curation (KYC'd borrowers, jurisdiction checks). No XRPL product offers this — institutional capital sits idle.

title: Native yield aggregator (Yearn-XRPL)
description: Cross-protocol yield routing for XRPL natively
problem_en: XRPL yield is fragmented across AMM, lending, vaults. Users juggle multiple protocols to find best yield. A Yearn-equivalent aggregator would auto-route capital, improving UX and yields.

title: XRPL DeFi position aggregator (DeBank-equivalent)
description: Cross-protocol dashboard aggregating user DeFi positions across AMM, lending, vaults on XRPL + EVM Sidechain
notes: Added from Djason interview — "Position DeFi introuvable" friction
problem_en: Users with DeFi positions across AMM, lending, vaults can't see them aggregated. Each protocol has its own UI. DeBank/Zapper serve EVM chains. XRPL needs equivalent to make DeFi positions visible and manageable. (Source: Djason interview)

title: Physical-to-Digital Binding (EU DPP)
description: Regulatory deadline — 12-month EU DPP window
problem_en: EU Digital Product Passport regulation requires every product to have a digital twin by 2027. No XRPL-native binding pattern exists despite XRPL's NFT primitives being ideal. 12-month regulatory window.

title: Yield-Bearing Stablecoin (T-bill backed)
description: USDe parallel — top community demand
problem_en: Users want stablecoin yield without DeFi risk. USDe (Ethena) raised $4B+ proving demand. No XRPL equivalent despite RLUSD being live and T-bill backing being trivially implementable.

title: Non-USD Stablecoin DeFi Rails
description: EUR/BRL/SGD/AUD rails
problem_en: Most XRPL DeFi assumes USD. EUR/BRL/SGD/AUD stablecoins exist but lack rails to integrate into lending, AMMs, vaults — locking out non-US users from native-currency DeFi.

title: Chunked Data + On-Chain Anchoring Pattern
description: IPFS/S3/self-hosted with on-chain anchoring
problem_en: Large data (legal docs, media files) can't fit on XRPL. Builders piecemeal-solve with IPFS/S3 + manual anchoring. A standard pattern would unify the approach and unlock data-heavy use cases.

title: RWA Issuance Studio EU/MiCA
description: MPT + DID + cap table — A1 Tier 1 #2
notes: Vertical illustrations: PropTok (real estate) in builder-atlas
problem_en: Tokenizing RWA in EU requires MiCA-compliant issuance (MPT + DID + cap table). No XRPL studio offers turnkey EU-compliant tokenization — each issuer rebuilds the legal/tech stack.

title: Regional POS / merchant tooling
description: Retail merchants in emerging markets + EU/MiCA
notes: Vertical illustration: MerchantPay blueprint
problem_en: Emerging markets merchants (Africa, LATAM) want crypto payment terminals. Existing solutions don't support XRPL. Regional POS with EU/MiCA compliance opens 100M+ underbanked users.

title: Gaming utility-NFT framework
description: Play-to-earn + asset interop — XRPL NFT primitives
problem_en: Game devs need NFT primitives for play-to-earn (items, achievements, cross-game assets). XRPL has NFT support but no game-specific framework — devs build from scratch every time.

title: Mid-market corporate bonds
description: On-chain mid-market corporate bond marketplace (BondBloc blueprint)
notes: Added Phase 1 — matches BondBloc blueprint
problem_en: Mid-market companies ($10M–$500M revenue) can't easily issue corporate bonds. Investment banks won't touch sub-$100M issuances. On-chain bond issuance with MiCA compliance opens a $T market.

title: RWA structuring firm (AI service)
description: AI agent + lawyer-on-tap that structures RWA tokenization for clients
notes: Added Phase 1 — service company distinct from M-16b (product/studio)
problem_en: Tokenizing RWAs (real estate, bonds, art) requires legal structuring, SPVs, custody. An AI agent + lawyer-on-tap service can handle structuring at 80-90% margin vs traditional Big Law $500/hr.

title: Restaking Protocol for XRP (Babylon-fork)
description: $110B+ XRP cap underutilized
problem_en: $110B+ XRP market cap sits idle. Babylon proved restaking is a major DeFi primitive. XRPL has no equivalent — capital can't be productively re-deployed beyond staking/holding.

title: Synthetic Assets / CDP Protocol (× Axiom)
description: Gold/stocks/forex synthetic assets
problem_en: Users want exposure to gold, stocks, forex on-chain. Synthetix/Axiom proved demand. EVM Sidechain has no synthetic-asset protocol — users go to Ethereum and bridge back.

title: Perpetual DEX (vAMM or order book)
description: Derivatives = highest volume DeFi — XRPL at zero
problem_en: Derivatives = highest-volume DeFi category globally. XRPL has zero perpetual DEXs. Traders go to Hyperliquid/dYdX. Without perps, XRPL DeFi will plateau at spot only.

title: Decentralized Insurance Protocol
description: Maturity signal for institutional adoption
notes: Distinct from S-08 (AI underwriting service that can feed it)
problem_en: Institutional DeFi adoption requires insurance against smart contract risk. Nexus Mutual/InsurAce serve Ethereum but no XRPL equivalent. Institutional capital won't allocate without insurance.

title: Prediction markets infrastructure
description: Engine layer · Polymarket equivalent
problem_en: Polymarket made $3B+ on US elections alone. The infrastructure for prediction markets (oracle resolution, market creation, settlement) is missing on XRPL/EVM Sidechain.

title: Prediction markets dApps (consumer)
description: Polymarket-style for politics/sports/crypto
problem_en: Once infrastructure exists, consumer-facing prediction dApps (politics, sports, crypto events) are the user-facing product. Polymarket-style UX on XRPL captures share Polymarket can't reach.

title: DeFi underwriting / insurance (AI service)
description: AI agent prices DeFi risk and underwrites for insurance protocols
notes: Added Phase 1 — service distinct from M-20 (insurance protocol)
problem_en: DeFi insurance protocols need underwriting expertise to price risk. AI agents trained on historical exploit data can underwrite programmatically at 70-90% margin vs human actuaries.

title: Pre-Deployed Testnet Infrastructure
description: Multiplier across everything — sandbox · SurfPool-equivalent (Solana parallel)
problem_en: Builders waste weeks setting up testnet environments, deploying canonical contracts, seeding test data. Devs also lack a SurfPool-equivalent local node (XRPL forces shared testnet — slow, flaky, replay-unfriendly). Solana has SurfPool, Ethereum has Anvil/Hardhat; XRPL is a productivity outlier. A pre-deployed sandbox + local node combo would multiply velocity across the entire ecosystem. (Confirmed in Djason interview, May 2026)

title: XRPL Capabilities Registry
description: Auto-update XLS feed — solves awareness gap
problem_en: XLS amendments are announced in scattered forums. Builders don't know which features are live, in vote, or proposed. A real-time registry would solve the awareness gap that's the #1 blocker per PWG analysis.

title: Vendor-Neutral Oracle / Bridge / Ramp Adapters
description: Zero-code-change provider swap (lib for app builders)
notes: Distinct from gap-12 (data marketplace for buyers)
problem_en: Switching from one oracle (Pyth) to another (Chronicle) requires code rewrites. Same for bridges and fiat ramps. Vendor-neutral adapters would let builders swap providers without code change.

title: CeDeFi Yield Integration SDK (CEX channel)
description: 60%+ XRP on CEX — #1 distribution play
problem_en: 60%+ of XRP sits on centralized exchanges (Binance, Bybit, Coinbase). DeFi yield is locked away from this majority. An SDK letting CEXs route XRP into XRPL DeFi = #1 distribution play.

title: P-256 / secp256r1 Signing (XLS proposal)
description: Cross-cutting — Apple Secure Enclave + WebAuthn + HSM
problem_en: Apple Secure Enclave + WebAuthn + most HSMs use P-256 keys. XRPL only supports secp256k1 and ed25519 — blocking Apple-device-native signing and enterprise HSM integration.

title: AgentPay — x402 + XRPL settlement
description: AI agent payments facilitator — programmatic infra
notes: Merged with gap-07 + AgentPay blueprint
problem_en: AI agents need to make payments. x402 (Cloudflare) is the emerging payment protocol but lacks XRPL settlement. AgentPay would bridge x402 + XRPL near-zero fees, capturing agent economy spend.

title: AI-Native Compliance Ops (service company)
description: YC RFS lens — also Service-01
notes: Merged with service-01
problem_en: Compliance is expensive (lawyers, KYC vendors, manual reviews). YC RFS thesis: an AI agent + lawyer-on-tap can deliver compliance-as-a-service at 70-90% margin. No XRPL-native compliance service exists.

title: AI-Native Treasury Ops (RLUSD automation)
description: A1 service-thesis — also Service-02 Treasury-aaS
notes: Merged with service-02
problem_en: Treasuries on XRPL need automated RLUSD management (rebalancing, yield optimization, payments scheduling). No AI-native treasury service exists despite XRPL's multisig+RegularKey being ideal for agent-controlled treasury.

title: AI-Native Restaking Manager (yield optimizer)
description: A1 service-thesis · auto-rebalance
problem_en: Restaking yield optimization requires constant rebalancing across protocols. Humans can't do this manually. An AI service that auto-rebalances would extract maximum yield with minimal user effort.

title: Onchain Reputation for AI Agents (KYA)
description: A1 service-thesis · agent identity layer
problem_en: As AI agents proliferate, counterparties need to verify agent identity and history (KYA = Know Your Agent). No XRPL reputation primitive exists — agents can't build verifiable track records.

title: Monitoring & B2B alerting
description: XRPL's Tenderly — B2B alerting product with UI
notes: Type changed BLOCK→APP (Tenderly-style product). S-06 is the AI-service variant
problem_en: XRPL has no Tenderly/Forta-equivalent. B2B teams running production XRPL ops are blind to issues until customers complain. Reactive support, not proactive alerting.

title: Market-making-as-a-Service
description: AI agent provides liquidity · 70-90% margin
problem_en: New tokens lack liquidity at launch. Manual market-making is expensive (specialists). AI agents can provide liquidity programmatically with 70-90% margin vs traditional MMs' 30-40%.

title: Community-ops-as-a-Service
description: AI agent runs Discord + Twitter + grants ops
problem_en: Crypto projects need 24/7 community management (Discord, grants, Twitter). Humans cost $80k+/year. An AI agent service delivers 24/7 at fraction of cost.

title: Dispute resolution & recovery
description: AI agent handles claims · refunds · recovery
problem_en: Crypto transactions are irreversible — but disputes still happen (mistaken sends, scams, malicious actors). No service handles claims, refunds, and recovery on-chain. Lost funds = lost users.

title: AI trading agents (DCA · momentum · alpha)
description: Quant agents on XRPL · alpha generation
problem_en: Retail traders want algorithmic strategies but can't write them. AI trading agents on XRPL — pre-built (DCA, momentum) or custom (alpha) — democratize sophisticated trading.

title: Agent treasury + wallet for AI
description: Wallet/treasury infrastructure for AI agents — 3rd layer of agent stack (with M-26 payments + M-30 identity)
notes: Added Phase 1 — distinct from M-26 (payments) and M-30 (identity)
problem_en: AI agents need a wallet they control programmatically with proper guardrails (spending limits, multisig overrides, audit logs). No XRPL-native agent wallet exists despite XRPL's multisig + RegularKey being ideal.

title: Data marketplace · oracle aggregator
description: Multi-source oracle aggregator + data marketplace for data buyers
notes: Added Phase 1 — distinct from M-23 (vendor-neutral adapters)
problem_en: Data buyers (devs, traders) need access to varied feeds (price, weather, sports, custom). No XRPL marketplace exists where data sellers and buyers meet. Devs are stuck with one oracle and a contract.

title: Audit & continuous monitoring (AI service)
description: AI service that continuously audits client protocols
notes: Added Phase 1 — service distinct from G-02 (B2B tooling)
problem_en: Smart contract audits cost $50-200k and are one-shot (state at audit time). Continuous monitoring requires expensive human teams. AI-based continuous audit delivers fresh insights at 80%+ margin.

title: AI agent credit card with RLUSD spending
description: Credit-card-like primitive for AI agents to spend RLUSD with guardrails — XRPL equivalent of OpenClaw on Solana
notes: Added from Djason interview — OpenClaw parallel
problem_en: AI agents need a credit-card-like primitive to spend RLUSD with guardrails. Solana has OpenClaw. XRPL has no equivalent despite multisig + RegularKey being ideal for agent-controlled spending. (Source: Djason interview)
